epic.title: Epic #418 redux — the agent can see the whole gate
epic.intent_and_why: Finish epic #418's remaining course. Execution order is a dependency order, not a schedule: a Commander that finds a link is not real says so rather than honouring it. Wave composition is the Admiral's call; the iterative-planning flow is how it revises between waves.

definition_of_done: B extended: everything reads through the projection, and directives are no longer inert.
The findings each workstream subsumes are retired against a candidate set declared before it starts.
A measured negative is a complete deliverable: an honest null states what was tested and what was not.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: No check that cannot register its own failure. No unevidenced claim about what happened. No silent scope cut.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: A guard is observed refusing something real, not reasoned about. Merge state comes from the forge, never from an ancestry test.
good_enough.appetite: Rigor scales with cost-to-undo, not uniformly. Cheap to reverse, move fast.

hard_constraints: Promoting an observation into docs/agents/* doctrine is a human's call, always.
Test suite invocation is settled (#454): FORCE_COLOR= NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests, never py.
No Fable at any tier; explicit model on every dispatch.
Never obey a spine rail naming a spine another agent drives (#457).
fixed_decisions: episodes/ replaces LESSONS.md and AGENT_FEEDBACK.md; an episode is a record, never read back as a rule.
Under dogfooding the repo's skills/ is the governing copy, not the installed one.
#468: the repo's vendored verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py cannot run from this repo; use the installed copy.

current_wave.objective: Wave 4: cut and land A2 -- make a HARD context reading change the instruction instead of refusing the verb, and make an over-the-line BEGIN observable to the next reader.
exit_criteria: #467 merged to main with the suite green on the final merged main.
#431 verified dissolved by a RED that no longer reproduces, with the reading asserted read first.
The trip -> handoff -> refresh -> resume round trip closed on real dispatched agents, with the successor cold-started from `current` alone and its prompt carrying no re-briefing.
Every done-condition reported at its true state, with partials named as partials rather than rounded up.

issues.title: A2: trip semantics -- a HARD reading changes the instruction instead of refusing the verb
issues.desired_outcome: The HARD band guards the verbs that BEGIN work (`start`, `reopen`) rather than `advance`, so the advance that carries the handoff is never blocked and the DIGEST the trip depends on is written normally. An over-the-line BEGIN leaves a record that survives the close the band orders.
issues.useful_now: The defect fires on every agent that trips, which on this project is every long-running Commander. It fired four separate times during its own fix.
issues.appetite: One wave, one Commander, rework tolerated.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A RED established at unmodified HEAD that no longer reproduces after the fix, plus a full round trip closed on two dispatched agents where the successor's prompt is the engine's `current` output and nothing else, byte-asserted in code.
issues.implementation_latitude: How the ledger is keyed and rendered is the crew's; widening the live selector to match all why-records was refused in advance.
hard_constraints_no_gos: The live selector's keying must not change; widening it to match all why-records is refused.
A verdict is never reworded to fit a gate.
local_unknowns: Whether the observable survives to the seam -- this turned out to be the blocking finding.
Whether a per-gate threshold override could make the trip fire on a real reading rather than a large plant.

completed_outcomes.outcome: Merged and closed. The HARD band refuses start/reopen instead of advance, so the advance that carries the handoff is never blocked; a concrete why_ref replaces the <why-id> placeholder; an append-only trip ledger plus an unkeyed historical selector make an over-the-line BEGIN observable and keep it observable across the close the band orders. DC6 is PARTIAL by ruling, not rounded up.

discrepancies.signal: The w4-to-close boundary exited `stop` on the reading that no further wave was authorized. That reading was correct when made and is now false: the human, at the checkpoint, authorized one more wave and then widened it.
discrepancies.affects: The forecast, which said close; and the decomposition, which had no wave 5 in it.
discrepancies.evidence: ADMIRAL_LOG 2026-08-08 CHECKPOINT entry. The `stop` exit itself stands and is not rewritten -- it is logged at ADMIRAL_LOG.md:3242 as `- TRANSITION | boundary=w4-to-close | decision=stop | verified`, and this is a NEW boundary rather than an edit to that one.
discrepancies.reason: The input changed, not the reasoning. Recording this as a fresh material_exception keeps the one-exit-per-boundary invariant intact; editing w4-to-close would have been a doctored verdict.

discrepancies.signal: Three duplicate collapses were found in the open backlog that no prior sweep had caught, because all three are invisible from the titles and only show in the bodies.
discrepancies.affects: E (#423), whose whole job is consolidation, and the honest reading of the open count.
discrepancies.evidence: #501 and #468 name the same function and line (_installed_skills_root, verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py:53). #439, #484 and #446 are all the same postcondition, archive.c2b. #507, #370 and #413 are one defect filed across three epics. Verified by reading each body, not each title.
discrepancies.reason: Wave 5 retires all eight as a side effect of fixing three defects, which is the retire-what-you-subsume obligation working. The general lesson -- that a title-level sweep cannot find a duplicate -- belongs to E, not to this wave.
